hook: A jasmonate signaling switch keeps maize tassels and ears in step, and breaking it delays silking
summary: In maize, a signaling module of ZmJAZ14 and ZmMYC2a/b controls genes for the flowering transition, ear initiation, and silk growth, so tassel and ear develop in sync. Disrupting it lengthens the gap between pollen shed and silk emergence, which hurts reproduction. The evolutionary-burden idea is a suggestion from genetics in maize, not a tested evolutionary claim.
title: The ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis-silking synchrony in maize.
